rows.finding: On all four delivered primary filings the flattener regenerated the CR-409 footer pushbutton captions and laid the long one out as a single line wider than its own widget and wider than the page: eight words lost off the left edge, three drawn inside the neighbouring Print button's rectangle, the sentence cut at both ends.
rows.rootCause: The finalizer had already classified all five CR-409 pushbuttons SUPPRESS_CONTROL_APPEARANCE and had already called the detachment. The detachment did not reach them. detachFromAcroForm in scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-active-content.mjs scanned only the AcroForm's own /Fields array, and ISO 32000-1 8.6.1 lets a field tree nest: CR-409's /Fields array holds ONE entry, `CR-409[0]`, and the four footer pushbuttons hang five /Kids levels below it. I confirmed this directly against data/rcap-all50/overlays/census-v1/ca/ca-851-91-set--official-pdf-fill/derived-sources/cr-409-pikepdf-unlocked.pdf: AcroForm /Fields size 1, the Warning[0] terminal field is not a member of it, and its parent chain is Warning[0] -> FooterButtons[0] -> MPLast[0] -> #pageSet[0] -> CR-409[0]. The scan therefore removed nothing and returned 0, form.getFields() still walked the field from the tree, updateFieldAppearances() regenerated its appearance from /MK /CA, and flatten() stamped it through the widget's own /P. That is the exact failure mode detachFromAcroForm's own comment warns about; it was simply blind to nesting.

whatIChanged.change: detachFromAcroForm now optionally walks the field tree: when the flat /Fields scan removes nothing, it removes the terminal field from its parent's /Kids and prunes interior nodes upward, including a root left empty in /Fields. Gated by walkFieldTree, default false. dropWidgets and restrictWidgetContributions pass the option through; sanitizeAndFlatten exposes it as detachNestedControlFields, default false.
